new_statements.rule_in_words: Kono is described as a two-level (H/L) tone language with five lexical tonal melodies over the CVCV foot; the sketch contains no statement about word stress or accent at all. (Same author, Jazyki mira 2017 p.286 §2.1.2, states for central Guinean Kpelle, of which she classes Kono as the eastern dialect: 'Фонологическое ударение в ГК отсутствует' = 'There is no phonological stress in Guinean Kpelle' -- but that description is explicitly scoped to the Honkwele variety of Nzerekore, not Kono.)
new_statements.exceptions: none (no stress discussion); tone: contextual mid tone in VP after H, downstep on ClV(ŋ) /H/ stems with 3sg prefix
new_statements.domain_note: Tonal melodies are lexical, assigned to morphemes/feet (CVCV); H spread domain is the syntactic phrase (VP, NP, PP). No word-stress domain is defined.
new_statements.identity_note: Konoshenko 2017 (Mandenkan 57) describes Kono of Lola prefecture, Forest Guinea (knu, kono1267), explicitly distinct from Kono of Sierra Leone (kno). Her Jazyki mira chapter (2017) instead classes the same lect (kɔ̀nɔ̌, 'eastern dialect') under Guinean Kpelle; the explicit no-stress sentence there (p.286 §2.1.2) is scoped to central Guinean Kpelle, Honkwele variety of Nzerekore (guin1254), not to Kono.
